messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need customer-facing language for last night’s outage and to confirm who owns follow-ups + when the external summary / RCA is appropriate.
Marta: I can draft a short status page blurb and an email for affected customers. timeline? aiming for EOD PDT?
Sam: EOD works if we lock the facts by 2pm. Ops can confirm the exact root cause then.
Emily: +1. Ops: is the technical RCA finalized enough to share with customers, or do we need a redacted summary first?
Jeff: We still have one lingering perf metric to verify (KV cache edge-case). That might change the mitigation wording. ETA ~90m.
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-23T01:12:27Z: engineering has attached the initial postmortem draft https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-4172
Marta: Thanks bot. I'll start with neutral, action-oriented language. draft snippet: "We experienced elevated request latency for ~45 minutes affecting API endpoints in us-west. Root cause: upstream network flapping -> degraded cache warm-up. Remediation: config rollback + longer-lived caches; full RCA to follow." Thoughts?
Alex: That reads well. Two asks: 1) call out customer impact (failed / retried requests, possible duplicate responses) 2) be explicit on data exposure (none)
Sam: Confirmed: no customer data was exfiltrated. Also add link to support doc for customers to retry safely.
Marta: OK will add: "No customer data was exposed. If you saw partial/duplicate responses, please retry; contact support" + link.
Emily: On RCA sharing policy: for enterprise customers on contracts, legal asks that we share the full RCA. For public_statuspage we should use a summarized version. We need to tag which customers get the detailed doc.
Jeff: Agree. Also recommend a 2-step publish: 1) status page + customer email summary (public-friendly) 2) full detailed RCA to contracts/legal/affected custs by next business day.
Alex: Who owns step 2? Product or Support?
Marta: Product can own the public drafts. Support / Solutions should own the targeted distribution to customers (they have the contact lists). I'll coordinate.
Sam: Action items: 
- Sam: finalize root cause and remediation paragraph (by 2:00pm PT)
- Marta: publish status page + customer email draft (by 5:00pm PT)
- Support (Emily): prepare list of affected customers and distribution plan (by COB)
- Alex: review + approve public copy (by 4:30pm PT)
Jeff: I'll follow up on the recurring pattern note: this is the 3rd network-flap incident in us-west Q1. Recommend a follow-up deep-dive to propose infra changes (owner: Jeff, due next Wed).
Emily: Also suggest adding a monitoring alert that counts similar flaps over 7d so we catch recurrence faster.
Alex: Good. For transparency: public summary should include a line about "we're scheduling a deeper reliability review" — keeps customers informed.
Marta: Draft status line updated with that. Will post the draft to #incidents-drafts for review shortly.
Sam: Once I confirm the final metric, I’ll paste the exact timeline snippet (start/end + retries count).
Emily: Support will prepare templated email and attach the full RCA when cleared by legal.
incident-bot: Reminder: please assign follow-up tasks in the incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4172/actions
Alex: Nice. Let's keep comms concise and avoid blaming 3rd parties explicitly. Focus on impact, root cause summary, mitigation, and next steps.
Marta: Posted draft to #incidents-drafts: https://slack.redwood/internal/archives/INC-4172/draft — please comment inline.
Jeff: I'll open the deep-dive ticket and assign to infra. Link will go into the postmortem.
Alex: Thanks all. We'll reconvene if any of the facts change. Otherwise plan: public summary tonight, full RCA to affected customers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
